question: Should OpenClaw adopt `@openclaw/localization-core` and `OPENCLAW_LOCALE` as supported cross-surface locale contracts through this ordered five-PR series, or keep localization scoped to existing surface-owned implementations?
rationale: This decision defines durable locale precedence, an operator-visible environment surface, package ownership, and the merge order of a broad feature series; implementation review alone cannot choose that product contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow shared contract
options.body: Approve a documented locale precedence and ownership boundary in the foundation PR, then require each later slice to consume only that boundary.

options.title: Keep localization surface-owned
options.body: Decline the shared package and retain or improve localization independently within the CLI, Control UI, and channel owners.

options.title: Pause the series pending RFC direction
options.body: Wait for explicit RFC review before accepting new locale overrides, registry ownership, and cross-surface presentation contracts.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow shared contract
recommendation.body: Approve a documented locale precedence and ownership boundary in the foundation PR, then require each later slice to consume only that boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC-linked series and can clarify the intended contract before maintainers make the acceptance decision.
